acceptance: A stub `zmx` records its argv, streams canned output and exits with a chosen code; a stub `systemd-run` records its argv and execs. Tests, red before the wrapper exists: dotted attach gets --labels with project and id before the name; undotted attach is untouched; run gets state=working then done; failed run exits with the task code and writes state=failed; ZMX_RAW=1 leaves argv byte-identical; a missing systemd-run falls back to bare zmx; an existing session is not relabelled; aliases a/r/l behave; `run` from inside a session resolves `.` to ZMX_SESSION. No real zmx and no real systemd are executed.
body: Modelled on dl-zmx-test: assert the argv a caller would build, never the environment it runs in. That is what makes these runnable in the jail (c-devjail). Keep the stubs in the test directory, named `zmx` and `systemd-run`, first on PATH.
title: Write the argv tests against stub binaries
